headline: Growth accelerates, losses narrow, guidance raised
summary_short: Revenue rose 33.5% year-over-year to $1,391M, with product revenue up 33.9% on continued consumption growth (net revenue retention of 126%); the operating loss narrowed to $326M from $447M a year ago and diluted EPS improved to -$0.86 from -$1.29.
summary_long: Product revenue growth was driven by higher consumption among existing customers, with net revenue retention holding at 126%. Cost of product revenue rose on higher third-party cloud/AI-inference spend, though product gross margin held flat at 71%. Sales & marketing fell to 42% of revenue (from 44%) and R&D to 39% (from 46%); G&A dropped $80.9M as last year's $106.5M San Mateo office-impairment charge didn't recur, narrowing the operating loss to $326M. Remaining performance obligations reached ~$9.2B (+38% y/y). Snowflake raised full-year FY2027 product-revenue guidance to $5,840M (from $5,660M) and guided Q2 FY2027 product revenue to $1,415-1,420M. The company repurchased $300M of stock in the quarter; cash and investments stood at $4.4B.

drivers.explanation: Consumption-driven product revenue growth and the absence of last year's one-time office-impairment charge narrowed losses; management raised full-year revenue and margin guidance.
primarily due to increased consumption of our platform by existing customers
Product gross margin held flat at 71% as lower personnel costs and higher cloud volume discounts offset costs from newly launched capabilities not yet at scale.
G&A fell $80.9M as a $106.5M prior-year asset-impairment charge tied to the San Mateo office exit didn't recur; sales & marketing and R&D both grew slower than revenue.
Net loss narrowed in line with the smaller operating loss; the effective tax rate was 0.4% versus a 1.4% benefit a year earlier.
EPS improved roughly in line with the narrower net loss, partly offset by a higher weighted-average diluted share count (345.4M vs 332.7M shares a year ago).
Company notes Q1 and Q4 are typically its strongest free-cash-flow quarters from order-timing seasonality; the sequential drop from Q4's elevated figure is not further explained in the filing.
Reflects the same existing-customer consumption growth cited for product revenue; the filing does not separately explain the quarter-over-quarter uptick.
Customer count grew to 13,912 from 13,296; the filing does not break out gross additions versus attrition.
